podcast.body: This song was the Billboard year-end number one for 2003, described as having a "plainly descriptive title." Curtis Jackson, known as 50 Cent, broke through with a hyped backstory of surviving multiple gunshots and ruling the mixtape circuit, but the song's "undeniable beat" was key. It spent eight weeks at number one, outlasting Beyoncé's "Crazy in Love" and Sean Paul's "Get Busy." "But none of that would have mattered if Indy Club didn't have such an undeniable beat."

podcast.body: This popular song was among those frequently converted into polyphonic ringtones during the mid-2000s. These ringtones, costing around two euros per message, were a key part of the burgeoning digital catalog industry, long before the advent of Spotify or iTunes. "cuáles eran estas canciones? Pues las que más lo petaban en esa época, Tok, In the Club, Bring Me Too Life o In Dien."
